1.mascotDialogue: The pivot does not move again after partitioning, beta — it is already home! Everything left to sort is strictly smaller on one side, strictly bigger on the other. Neat and settled.

2.mascotDialogue: Line 9 places the pivot at its final resting index, beta. Lines 16 and 17 then recurse on the strictly-smaller and strictly-larger sides — the pivot itself? Never touched again, not once.

3.mascotDialogue: This pivot happened to be the smallest value, beta, so it ends up all the way at index 0 — an unlucky pivot choice! And a very good example of why pivot selection actually matters for performance.

4.mascotDialogue: One character off, beta — p instead of p minus 1 — and the recursion loses its most important guarantee: that every recursive call works on a strictly smaller range than the one before. One character, whole guarantee gone!
